jobs.occupation: VPP Operations Specialist – Germany (m/w/d) (Bau- und Projektkaufmann/-frau)
jobs.description:
What to Expect

We are scaling our Virtual Power Plant (VPP) operations into the German energy market and are looking for a hands-on VPP Operations Specialist – Germany to support that growth from day one. We need someone who can roll up their sleeves, own exceptions end-to-end, and bring deep practical knowledge of how the German energy market operates at a process and regulatory level.You will be embedded in our Operations team, working closely with our flexibility, settlements, and support functions across the globe. A key part of your role will be upskilling our support staff on German market workflows, participant journeys, and exception handling – ensuring the whole team can operate confidently as we grow our German footprint.

What You’ll Do

Market Operations

- Apply working knowledge of the German energy regulatory landscape (BNetzA, BDEW) to day-to-day operational tasks.
- Manage and resolve data flow exceptions relating to MaKo/EDIFACT messaging, GPKE, and WiM processes, and MSB/VNB interactions.
- Support the accurate management of MaLo and MeLo data, ensuring data integrity across systems.
- Work within the MsbG metering framework and support smart meter rollout processes relevant to VPP-connected assets.
- Demonstrate solid understanding of MaBis processes.
- Monitor Bilanzkreis and settlement obligations relevant to our flexible asset portfolio in Germany.Flexibility Participant & Exception Management
- Act as the primary handler for escalated exceptions arising from the German flexibility participant journey – from asset registration through to settlement and payment queries.
- Own complex cases end-to-end, coordinating across internal teams (settlements, tech, finance) to reach resolution.
- Identify recurring issues and escalate systemic root causes with clear data and recommended fixes.
- Support onboarding of new German flexibility participants and asset owners, ensuring a smooth and compliant process.Training & Knowledge Transfer
- Design and deliver structured training sessions for UK-based support staff covering German market processes, regulatory obligations, and participant workflows.
- Build and maintain clear, practical playbooks, process guides, and FAQs for use by the wider support team.
- Conduct regular knowledge gap assessments and adjust training content accordingly.
- Review training effectiveness and iterate based on team performance and feedback.Process Improvement & Efficiency
- Actively identify manual or repetitive tasks and find ways to reduce effort through process redesign or tooling.
- Maintain up-to-date process documentation in a clear, accessible format.
- Flag regulatory or process changes in the German market that may impact operations and recommend responses.

What You’ll Bring

Candidates should be able to demonstrate practical working knowledge across most of the following:

- BNetzA regulatory framework and BDEW market rules
- MaKo communication standards and EDIFACT message types
- GPKE (supplier switching) and WiM (metering point management) processes
- MsbG obligations and the role of the Messstellenbetreiber (MSB)
- MaLo (market location) and MeLo (metering location) data structures
- Bilanzkreis management and balancing group settlement
- German electricity billing structures including Netzentgelte and Grundversorgung vs. competitive supply frameworks
- Direktvermarktung framework
- MaBis processes for balancing group settlement reconciliation
- FCR/aFRR/mFFR prequalification and flexibility market participation rules (desirable)Essential
- Fluent in English and German (written and spoken), with experience communicating with German counterparts and producing documentation in both languages
- Demonstrable hands-on experience working within the German energy market at an operational level (a minimum of 3 years)
- Proven ability to manage exceptions and complex operational cases end-to-end
- Experience designing and delivering training or knowledge transfer programmes
- Strong analytical mindset with a practical, solutions-first approach
- Comfortable working autonomously and picking up tasks without needing close directionDesirable
- Experience with MaKo-compliant systems or EDIFACT messaging tools
- Knowledge of MSB obligations and smart meter rollout processes in Germany
- Experience working across multiple European energy markets
- Experience in a scale-up or market entry environment

Professional Experience:

What to Expect

Tesla is seeking an Account Manager for residential energy sales for Germany. Your core responsibility is B2B sales of Tesla residential and small commercial energy products in Germany, with the focus of selling our Powerwall product, a home battery designed to store energy from solar and/or the grid. You will develop, maintain, and grow a productive customer network, such as distributors and 3rd party installers. In addition, you will actively drive business development opportunities in your region. We are looking for an experienced commercial professional with working experience in the PV or energy storage industry.  In addition to a strong work ethic and a team-oriented personality, successful team members exhibit creativity, passion, and a drive to pioneer advancements in an ever-evolving technological and market landscape.

- Evaluate new business opportunities with current and new accounts and/or sales channels, identify suitable product offerings, and take ownership of capturing these opportunities 
- Deliver key market insights into the broader business team 
- Provide sales forecasts to business and manufacturing teams,  
- Support evaluating market dynamics across sectors (utility, commercial & industrial, residential, etc.) and drivers (policy/regulatory, economics, etc.)  
- Represent Tesla at sales and marketing events promoting Powerwall 
- Help identify and support implementation of initiatives to maintain or improve partner training, partner installation quality, and to improve Tesla operations and fulfilment and Tesla support 
- Provide user / customer feedback to IT development teams regarding Tesla tools, systems and to Operations regarding processes 

What You’ll Bring

- 5+ years of work experience in an account management/channel sales role within the PV, energy storage industry
- Excellent communication and documentation skills 
- Ability to prioritize work and execute many projects and tasks in parallel 
- Working knowledge of grid/utility markets, as well as grid-tied technologies 
- Fluency in English and German

jobs.occupation: 573787 Business Marketing Manager IGT-Devices (all genders) (Betriebswirt/in (Hochschule) - Marketing)
jobs.description:
To support our initiatives for further adoption of Philips technology providing Class IA guideline treatment options, we are expanding our International marketing team with a Business Marketing Manager DACH, responsible for the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio.

The Business Marketing Manager is the dedicated field-based marketing owner for the DACH market zone, covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland. This role is accountable for translating international and global marketing strategy into locally relevant market activation, demand generation and adoption across the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio. The individual is expected to operate close to the market, spending significant time in the field with sales teams, customers, clinical partners and regional stakeholders to understand local needs, identify growth opportunities and remove barriers to execution.

The role combines strategic portfolio marketing with hands-on field execution. The Business Marketing Manager will define and drive DACH-specific marketing plans, shape customer engagement programs, support priority account activation, build local proof points and ensure launches, campaigns and market development initiatives are executed with strong local relevance and commercial impact.

As a member of the International Marketing team, you will own specific marketing activities that span the complete international region.

Success in this role requires regular travel and visible presence across the zone. The individual should expect to travel extensively within DACH, approximately 50-60% of time, to engage with customers, KOLs, sales teams, professional societies, congresses, workshops and other in-market activation opportunities.

Your role:

Own the DACH market zone

- Act as the primary marketing owner for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, accountable for local market planning, activation priorities and execution quality. Be present in the field with sales team, and customers to understand adoption barriers, customer needs, competetive dynamics and local growth opportunities.
- Collaborate with global and international marketing, market intelligence, and sales leadership to prioritise target accounts, market segments, and growth opportunities across the portfolio.
- Lead specific marketing capabilities internationally, strengthening the broader International marketing organization.
- Translate strategy into local execution by converting global and international portfolio strategies into DACH-specific messaging, campaigns, engagement formats and sales enablement priorities.
- Drive demand generation and adoption by leading marketing activities that increase awareness, utilization and customer preference for the full IGTD portfolio.

Partner internally, externally and represent the voice of the market

- Partner with sales leadership and field teams to prioritize accounts, shape plans, refine messaging and support commercial objectives.
- Bring structured market insights, customer feedback and competitive intelligence back to the international marketing team to influence activation planning and portfolio priorities.
- Seek and develop opportunities to strengthen Philips’ cardiology value proposition for customers in your region by close partnership with adjacent Philips categories such as the One-IGT unique solution offering.
- Build reference sites, customer testimonials, and clinical proof points that resonate with local audiences. Partner with KOLs and professional societies to strengthen Philips’ position in focus markets.
- Work under limited supervision and broad guidelines, serving as the primary marketing contact for assigned portfolio areas and focus markets.
- Define proposals for the mid-term marketing strategy, identifying key market challenges and opportunities early and implementing business plans and goals accordingly.

You're the right fit if:

- Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Healthcare, or related field.
- 3–5 years of experience in downstream marketing, preferably in healthcare, medtech, or related industries.
- Demonstrated experience managing a broad product and solutions portfolio (not limited to a single category or technology platform).
- Proven ability to lead dedicated market initiatives – owning the full marketing cycle from strategy to execution within specific geographies.
- Strong execution skills with the ability to adapt global strategies for local impact.
- Excellent presentation, communication, and stakeholder management abilities.
- Knowledge of image-guided therapy, interventional systems, or healthcare technology is a plus.
- Must be fluent in German and English languages.
- Willingness to travel 50–60% of time.

Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. The base salary range for this role is € 126,297.80 – € 159,977.21. We determine pay within the range using objective factors, like the skills the role requires, your relevant experience and the responsibility you will have in this role, alongside internal equity and local market considerations.

This role is eligible for Short Term Incentive, with your rewards linked to individual performance and company results. We will share the full approach with you during the interview process, so you can make a clear, informed decision.

Benefits include:

- Annual leave: 30 days
- Mobility and devices: subsidized Germany ticket, leasing opportunities for private use (bicycles, cars, smartphones, ...)
- Philips University & Philips in Balance: wide range of professional training courses for personal development and healthcare
- Philips Pension Fund: employer-funded pension plan
- Philips Partnerzeit: two paid weeks off after your partner has given birth
- Philips MyShop: discount on Philips products
- Culture: informal culture, a paid day for voluntary work, various team and cultural activities, etc.

How we work together
Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

About Philips
We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others.

jobs.description:
Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 November 2026:

Postdoc Researcher (m/f/d)

in Evolutionary Genomics of Mammals** (m/f/d)**

(Full time / part time** **options available)

﻿

Location: Frankfurt am Main
Employment scope: Full-time; part time options are available
Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 2 years
Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity and climate change.

There is an exciting opportunity for a talented and motivated applicant to join the working group of Prof. Dr. Axel Janke. The applicant will be closely involved in gene flow, evolutionary, population or phylo-genetics to study speciation in mammals (bears, giraffe, kangaroos or allies) at the genomic level and in MSc and BSc teaching. Strong own and proven research interests including other vertebrate groups will be considered.

Your tasks

- Conduct genomic research on mammalian evolution and speciation, including evolutionary, population and phylogenomic analyses
- Investigate phylogenetic relationships, gene flow and genomic signatures of evolutionary and environmental processes using genomic and bioinformatic approaches
- Apply and further develop bioinformatic methods for the analysis of genomic data, including population genomics, genome assembly and species distribution modelling
- Organise and teach university courses and supervise BSc and MSc theses
- Independently prepare and publish research results in peer-reviewed journals and contribute to the acquisition of third-party funding

Your profile

- PhD degree in Biology, Genetics, Bioinformatics or a related field
- Strong interest and proven skills in evolutionary, population or phylogenomics.
- Knowledge of gene-flow analyses and/or drift processes is an advantage
- Experience in population genomics, genome assembly and script programming, including R
- Very good written and oral communication skills in English
- Interest in species distribution modelling, paternal inference, conservation genetics and epigenetics

We offer

- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution
- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan

Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, gender, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply, as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.

How to apply?

- CV

- Contact details of two potential references

Please compress the files where possible. If the two publications cause the file to exceed the upload limit, they may be uploaded separately.

Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:

Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)

(full time / part time options available)

Location: Görlitz

Type of contract: initially limited to three years; 

the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluation

Remuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13

The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.

The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.

Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.

For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.

Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleagues

Your tasks

- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.
- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.
- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.
- Secure external research funds.
- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.
- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.
- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.
- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.

Your profile

- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups
- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context
- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations
- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage
- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management
- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team
- Very good command of German (B2)
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written
- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)
- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstances

Desirable skills 

- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology
- Knowledge in research data management and databases
- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum work

We offer 

- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations
- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology
